text:
Asha Patel: sharing a quick sketch of the form changes — question on error hierarchy: inline field errors vs a single top banner + brief toast for transient issues. Thoughts? Samir Liu: I lean inline for input-specific validation (required, pattern) so screen reader users get per-field context. Banner for form-level failures (submit failed server-side). Eli Gomez: Agree with Samir. Also want to call out visual noise: inline messages should be subtle and collapse when fixed. Banner should persist until user dismisses. Maya Chen: UX nit: where do we put the destructive action (Delete dataset) in the long form? Inline with other actions at the bottom, or in the header as a danger button? Asha Patel: header feels discoverable but could be accidentally clicked. If header, must be less prominent and require explicit confirm. Bottom placement reduces accidental clicks but is less visible. Samir Liu: Accessibility note — confirm modals need focus trap and clear purpose for screen readers. Prefer confirm dialog with explicit typed-confirm for irreversible deletes. Eli Gomez: Could we do a progressive safeguard: first click opens a compact inline section requiring typing the dataset name, not a modal? Less disruptive for keyboard users. Maya Chen: Hmm, inline typed-confirm helps flow but could be hard to discover for people used to modals. Maybe use inline reveal + `aria-live` announcement. Asha Patel: here's a minimal markup example for inline error + accessible hint we discussed: ```html
Required
``` Samir Liu: Small tweak: `role=\"alert\"` will announce on show, good. Add `aria-invalid=\"true\"` on the input when error present. Eli Gomez: For the destructive inline confirm pattern, we might do: ```html
Type the dataset name:
``` Maya Chen: Also include `aria-describedby` on the confirm input pointing to a short explanation like \"This action permanently removes X\". Asha Patel: Question for the group: visual affordance for required fields — asterisk only, or a \"Required\" hint under label? Asterisk is compact but ambiguous for some users. Samir Liu: I vote asterisk + screen-reader text `required` like your markup. Keeps visual density low but accessible. Eli Gomez: I'd be OK with an optional legend at the form top: \"* required\" for discoverability on complex forms. Maya Chen: Copy for the destructive confirm — prefer short explicit sentence: \"Type the dataset name to confirm deletion\" and button labeled \"Delete permanently\" (red) and a secondary \"Cancel\". DesignBot: Automated accessibility scan: `aria-describedby` present? yes. `aria-invalid` missing on input id=name. Recommend adding. Asha Patel: Thanks — I'll update the sketch: inline errors for field-level, banner for server errors, asterisk + sr-only required, typed-inline confirm for delete (with fallback modal for small screens). I'll post updated screens in ~30m. :thumbsup: Samir Liu: SGTM. One more: add small animation so inline errors don't shift layout (fade in), avoids focus jump. Eli Gomez: And add tests for screen reader flow in our e2e suite. Maya Chen: Great — excited to see the mock.
